title: Uric acid
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows your uric acid level. Too much of it can cause joint pain.
why: For painful, swollen joints, especially the big toe, for kidney stones, high blood pressure, or at a checkup.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come the next day
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially water pills
If you are already treated for gout
If you had joint pain attacks, and when the last one was

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting: no food for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 1 to 2 days, eat less meat, organ meats, and fish. No alcohol and no hard workouts.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

bring: Past test results, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 day. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Does high uric acid mean gout?
faq.a: Not always. The doctor diagnoses gout from your symptoms and an exam, not just the test.

faq.q: Can I take the test during an attack?
faq.a: Yes, but during an attack the level is sometimes normal. Your doctor may ask you to repeat it later.

reminders.text: Uric acid test tomorrow. No meat, fish, or alcohol today. Do not eat after dinner.
